title: Bias-Adjusted LLM Agents for Human-Like Decision-Making via Behavioral Economics
reasoning: The paper focuses on behavioral economics and aligning LLM agent decision-making with human behavior in economic games like the ultimatum game. While it discusses fairness and social preferences, it does so through the lens of game theory and behavioral traits (e.g., reciprocity, risk aversion) rather than evaluating religion, faith, or specific ethical/moral frameworks.
